clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with classic features of metabolic syndrome—obesity, severe dyslipidaemia, pre‑diabetic A1c, and hypertension—forming the central pathophysiologic driver. This cluster explains the elevated ASCVD risk, predisposes to NAFLD, and contributes to resistant hypertension. Concurrently, chronic daily opioid use for multisite musculoskeletal pain raises the likelihood of opioid‑use disorder and hyperalgesia. The current blood pressure (104/55 mmHg) on three antihypertensives suggests overtreatment, which may be compounding a subtle rise in BUN and potential early CKD. Obesity also makes obstructive sleep apnea probable. The differential prioritises metabolic syndrome as the primary diagnosis, followed by opioid‑related complications and medication‑related hypertension overtreatment, with secondary considerations for early diabetes, NAFLD, OSA, early CKD, and future ASCVD.

recommended_workup: Fasting lipid panel repeat after lifestyle intervention.
Serum creatinine, eGFR calculation, and urine albumin‑creatinine ratio.
Comprehensive iron studies (serum ferritin, transferrin saturation, reticulocyte count).
Liver function tests (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, bilirubin) and abdominal ultrasound or FibroScan for NAFLD assessment.
Thyroid panel (TSH, free T4) to evaluate hypothyroidism as a contributor to dyslipidaemia.
STOP‑BANG screening and, if positive, overnight polysomnography for obstructive sleep apnea.
Orthostatic vital signs and volume‑status assessment (urine sodium, clinical exam).
Opioid Risk Tool, urine drug screen, and structured opioid taper plan with multimodal pain management.
Wound assessment of the stage II pressure injury with culture if signs of infection appear.
ACC/AHA 10‑year ASCVD risk calculator (requires age, sex, race, cholesterol, BP, diabetes status, smoking).
PHQ‑9 and GAD‑7 questionnaires to screen for mood or anxiety disorders.
